overview: December 1949 airgram transmits a GHQ release on Japan's revised 1950 rapeseed-collection program, letting farmers retain part of their crop, substitute surplus rapeseed for wheat/barley quotas for meal, while dropping the rapeseed-oil return ration, aiming to boost output amid an edible-oil shortage.

subfiles.title: Airgram from Tokyo on revisions to Japan’s rapeseed-collection program
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser (USPOLAD), Tokyo; signed Sebald
subfiles.about: The airgram relays a General Headquarters news release describing changes to Japan’s rapeseed-collection rules for the 1950 crop.
subfiles.summary: GHQ announces Japanese farmers may retain part of their rapeseed harvest under a revised collection system to boost domestic output and cut import reliance; farmers may substitute rapeseed for wheat/barley quotas for meal, but lose the rapeseed-oil return ration.

interest: Shows a 1949 revised Japanese rapeseed-collection system to boost output amid edible-oil shortages.
